chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Asheym, from Safwan, who said:

A man asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) and I was present, so he said, 'I have an injury in my backside. So I perform Wudu and cleanse myself, then I find after that wetness and yellowness from the backside. Should I repeat the Wudu?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And you have purified it?' He said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. But, sprinkle water upon it and do not repeat the Wudu'.
Ahmad, from Abu Nasr, who said: 'A man asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) with approximately the Hadith of Safwan.'
ai.seo_question: What should one do with Wudu if they have an injury and find moisture after cleansing?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), the principle of *istibra’a* (ensuring the cessation of urine discharge) is applied to those with persistent injuries, establishing that once the primary impurity is removed, subsequent minor discharges do not invalidate Wudu. The Imam’s directive to merely sprinkle water (*rushshahu*) rather than repeating the full ablition highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on removing hardship (*raf’ al-haraj*) for the sick, distinguishing between the removal of the impurity itself and the ritual state of purity.
